name: Hammerhead
label: AmRep
lede: Three men from Fargo and Moorhead moved to Minneapolis and made three albums for [[Amphetamine Reptile Records]] before [[Paul Sanders]] left for college. They came back in 2010 for the label's 25th anniversary and kept going.

eras.title: Outsiders from Fargo, signed in Minneapolis
eras.text: Paul Sanders, Paul Erickson and Jeff Mooridian Jr. started out in Fargo and Moorhead, then moved to Minneapolis. Amphetamine Reptile Records had them on a 7" before there was an album.

years.big: "We were never welcomed into the hardcore scene."
years.h: "Peep" is Hammerhead's first single on AmRep
years.p: Sanders said that to City Pages about the band's Fargo-to-Minneapolis years. The "Peep" 7" came out on [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile Records in 1991, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp:
The trio first played together at a club called the Aquarium in Fargo, North Dakota. Sanders told City Pages that punk, hardcore and AmRep now look like one thing to a lot of people, "but at the time it wasn't."

Wikipedia lists "Peep" (1991) and "Load King" (1992) as the early 7" singles.

years.h: Ten songs in two days at Gark
years.p: Hammerhead cut their debut on October 3 and 4, 1992 at Gark studio in Minneapolis, with Chris Coyne at the board. It runs 32 minutes 42 seconds.
years.xp: David B. Livingstone is also credited on the recording and mixing. City Pages called the result an "unrelenting, rage-fueled debut." The Washington Post heard more than thump and squeal, noting that Sanders and Erickson occasionally trade vocals and even harmonize.

eras.title: A tribute, a tour with the Cows, two more records
eras.text: A Husker Du cover, a first major tour with Cows, the Evil Twin EP and then Into the Vortex, all between 1993 and early 1994.

years.p: The debut LP is out on Amphetamine Reptile Records. AllMusic and Wikipedia date it 1993, though one AmRep fan site says 1992, the year it was recorded.

years.h: Hammerhead cover Husker Du for a Zen Arcade tribute
years.p: Their "Something I Learned Today" is one of the tracks on the 1993 tribute Du Huskers, on which Minnesota bands covered all of Zen Arcade.

years.h: The Cows take Hammerhead on their first major tour
years.p: That was Jeff Mooridian Jr.'s name for it in City Pages. Sanders added that the Cows "were so far off of the map from anything else at the time."
years.xp: The [[Cows|d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b]] were AmRep's Minneapolis noise-rock veterans. City Pages doesn't say which dates the tour covered.

years.h: An EP, Evil Twin, gathers songs from 1991 to 1993
years.p: Seven songs, 18 minutes 42 seconds, out December 7 on AmRep. Wikipedia says the tracks were recorded between 1991 and August 1993, so it works as a singles round-up.

years.h: Into the Vortex comes out of AmRep's own studio
years.p: Tim Mac recorded it in January at Am Rep Recording Division in Minneapolis, with cover art by [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]. "Journey to the Center of Tetnus 4" runs 7:11, the longest of nine tracks.
years.xp: The album comes to 39 minutes 41 seconds. Wikipedia quotes the Portland Mercury calling it "one of the finest releases in the storied history of Amphetamine Reptile Records," and the Seattle Times saying the songs "explode like pop supernovas."
play: Journey to the Center of Tetnus 4

eras.title: One more album, then college
eras.text: A split 7" with Halo of Flies and a last album, Duh, the Big City. Paul Sanders left afterward and the trio ended in 1996.

years.h: Kat Bjelland of Babes in Toyland sings on "Camaro"
years.p: It's Hammerhead's side of the 1995 AmRep split 7" Porn No. 1 with [[Halo of Flies|3a26de45-4f41-4e28-bdc8-fda60ef0c8d0]], and it resurfaced on the 1996 Screwed soundtrack.

yt: Victoria, live at the AmRep 25th anniversary, 2010
years.h: The last album is Duh, the Big City
years.p: Eleven songs, recorded in 1995 at Beehive and Perma Sonics with Tim Mac. Erickson wrote most of it, Sanders wrote "Victoria" and the title track, and [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] did the cover.

years.h: Sanders trades the band for college and a paycheck
years.p: Paul Sanders left after Duh, the Big City to go to college and work. Nearly two decades later he told an interviewer what he thought of that decision.
years.xp:
In a 2014 interview with the Ice Planet blog, Sanders said he wanted a career and money for a while like a normal person, so he quit and went to college. He then played in Heroine Sheiks and Fly Republic and worked on More RAM.

Sources differ on timing: AllMusic and AmRep sites say he left in 1995, while Wikipedia and Sanders's own account put it after the 1996 album.

eras.title: Vaz in the middle, the trio back in 2010
eras.text: Paul Erickson and Jeff Mooridian Jr. formed the duo Vaz after Hammerhead. In 2010 all three were back, with a new EP the next year.

years.h: Erickson and Mooridian carry on as Vaz
years.p: With Sanders gone, bassist [[Paul Erickson|84245bbf-3baf-4f3a-be3b-217f62da5dd6]] and drummer [[Jeff Mooridian Jr.|b9f9930f-185f-419d-a8f2-5883cfcfe5ba]] formed [[Vaz|3edc106c-fb86-4c12-a616-5ebda994e399]], an experimental duo that later played on from New York.

yt: Earth (I Won't Miss), AmRep 25th anniversary, Minneapolis, 2010
years.h: AmRep's 25th anniversary brings the trio back
years.p: Hammerhead played Amphetamine Reptile Records' 25th anniversary show in Minneapolis, then shows at Death By Audio in Brooklyn.
years.xp:
The Janitor Joe page on Wikipedia dates the anniversary night to August 29, 2010 and lists Erickson in that band's one-night reunion for the same show. The fan-shot clip of "Earth (I Won't Miss)" is dated August 28 by its uploader.

Sanders later said they only wanted to get back together if they could move the band forward.

years.h: After 15 quiet years, the Memory Hole EP
years.p: The reunion produced an EP on Amphetamine Reptile Records in 2011. Sanders said recording across Brooklyn and Minneapolis was hard, but the band clicked again fast.
Wikipedia lists the reunion-era album New Directionz (2015), after the Global Depression EP (2014).
years.xp:
City Pages put Global Depression at about 15 minutes, recorded at Terrarium Studios in northeast Minneapolis. Erickson told the paper, "Half of my most interesting riffs are mistakes."

Sanders said writing takes them longer than other bands because they try a lot of different things.
